articles.headline: When will the Chargers finally win? Here are the odds and our best bets
articles.description: The Chargers are 0-8 heading into their Monday night matchup with the Ravens. If they don't win this week, when will they get off the schneid?
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers came into the 2026-27 season with Super Bowl aspirations. On opening night of the season, the Chargers were 17-1 to win the championship. Only the Los Angeles Rams (+500), Baltimore Ravens (10-1), Buffalo Bills (10-1), Seattle Seahawks (12-1) and Kansas City Chiefs (16-1) had shorter odds.

My, how things have changed. The Chargers enter Week 10 winless at 0-8 and are 1000-1 to win the Super Bowl. Offerings for them to make the playoffs are no longer even on the board. They have been outscored by 98 points, easily the worst differential in the league.

So when will win No. 1 come? According to the odds at DraftKings, the Chargers' best chance comes in Week 11 against the New York Jets (+125). Their second-best opportunity? That comes Monday night, when they are +185 to notch their first win against the Ravens. The Chargers are 4.5-point road underdogs, but FPI is more optimistic, giving them a 56.1% chance to win.

Things get a little dicier if they don't get out of the win column in the next two weeks.

If not now, when? We asked our betting analysts to give their predictions for when the Chargers would finally get off the schneid.

Week 11 vs. Jets (+125)

Pamela Maldonado: Miami is in the conversation, but that game is weeks away. The Jets are the best immediate opportunity. New York's defense doesn't create many of the problems that have wrecked the Chargers. The Jets struggle against the run and have intercepted just two passes. That should give Justin Herbert a cleaner game, one that can allow Omarion Hampton to carry more of the offense. It's difficult to trust the Chargers, but a matchup against the Jets asks far less of Herbert.

Eric Moody: The Chargers are 4.5-point road underdogs against the Ravens on Monday night but are already early 3-point home favorites against the Jets in Week 11. New York has lost five consecutive games and could be without Geno Smith, who suffered an ankle injury against the Bills on Sunday. Rookie Cade Klubnik could make his first NFL start. I expect the Chargers to lose in Baltimore, but I like Herbert's chances of getting Los Angeles its first win at home against a struggling 2-8 Jets team.

Liz Loza: The Chargers' offense hasn't done much well. However, Mike McDaniel's ground game has proved more productive than his aerial attack. Additionally, Herbert has posted numbers with his legs, ranking sixth at the position in rushing yards per game (23.8). That sets up well against a Jets defense that has struggled to stop the run and contain mobile signal callers.

Week 12 vs. Patriots (+500)

Matt Bowen: This New England Patriots' offense will regress with Tommy DeVito under center. He's a lower-level No. 2 quarterback. And A.J. Brown (hamstring) could be down again for the Week 12 matchup. Can the Chargers steal one here? Yes, if Herbert can play with better decision-making. Let's take the odds here.

articles.headline: Drake Maye ankle injury: Is the Patriots' season over? Can Tommy DeVito step up?
articles.description: If the QB doesn't return in 2026, New England faces an uphill battle against some of the NFL's best teams.
articles.body:
The outlook for the New England Patriots' 2026 season has been dramatically altered. After suffering an injury on the Patriots' first drive against the Detroit Lions on Sunday, quarterback Drake Maye did not fly back from Munich with the team out of caution, as the team is concerned he might have sustained a fractured ankle.

The 5-5 Patriots haven't been among the AFC's elite in 2026, but were hoping to make a charge to the playoffs -- and Maye potentially finding his past runner-up MVP form was one of their silver linings.

When Maye was taking care of the football and extending plays, the Patriots were explosive and flashed potential to hang with the best -- as a Week 4 win at the Buffalo Bills showed. But when Maye was not buttoned-up with his decision-making (he entered Sunday with 11 INTs), the Patriots struggled to get by some of the league's lower-echelon teams, with close wins against the New York Jets and Miami Dolphins, who have won a combined three games this season.

Coach Mike Vrabel often says it's hard to win when a team's best players don't play well, and simply put, Maye is the team's best offensive player.

Entering Week 10, he ranked top five in the NFL in Total QBR (74.2), passing touchdowns (18), yards per attempt (8.4), rushing yards by a quarterback (219) and rushing touchdowns by a quarterback (3).

Now potentially without Maye for weeks or even the season, the question is can the team make it back to the playoffs?

ESPN Patriots reporter Mike Reiss answers some of the top questions about the trickle-down effect of Maye's injury and analyst Matt Bowen answers a fantasy question on what to expect if you have Patriots players in your lineup.

Is the Patriots' 2026 season over?

When Vrabel was hired as head coach in January 2025, he said the team's goals were to win the division, host home playoff games and compete for championships. Their odds of doing that without Maye are closer to zero, starting with the current standings -- they are 5-5 while the AFC East rival Bills are 8-1.

Here is the rest of the Patriots schedule: they are on the bye in Week 11 before a road trip to face the winless Los Angeles Chargers, then two huge home games in a span of five days -- vs. the Bills (Dec. 6) and the Minnesota Vikings (Dec. 10). Then they're at the Kansas City Chiefs and the New York Jets before finishing the year with home games against the Denver Broncos and the Miami Dolphins.

They have played poorly the past two weeks in blowout losses to the Packers and Lions, ravaged by injuries across the roster, but Maye's presence -- even as he battled through inconsistent play with turnovers -- gave them a sliver of hope.

Consider what happened Sunday: After New England's opening drive when Maye was injured on the final play, they totaled seven points and gained 82 yards over 10 drives, averaging 1.9 yards per play (not including kneel down). New England punted on eight of those drives, with seven three-and-outs.

articles.headline: Packers' Matt LaFleur still plans on Micah Parsons to return on Thanksgiving eve
articles.description: The Packers still hope Micah Parsons will be ready to make his return for the Thanksgiving eve game at the Rams in Week 12.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Micah Parsons still has work to do to make his return from last year's knee injury in time for the Green Bay Packers' next game, but the hope is that the All-Pro edge rusher will be ready for the Thanksgiving eve game at the Los Angeles Rams in Week 12.

"Well, that's my plan," Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Monday. "I think my plan's been different than everyone else's this whole time. We'll see."

The Packers have been without Parsons since Week 15 of last year, when he tore the ACL and meniscus in his left knee. He took part in 11-on-11 drills in practice last week, although he missed one day due to an illness, after doing only individual drills the previous week, when the Packers opened his 21-day practice window while he's still on the physically unable to perform list.

"Obviously, having been in practice and banking some reps, there's still a couple more hurdles for him to clear before we can definitely say that he's a go," LaFleur added. "But he's been showing progress and we'll see where he's at by the end of the week."

Packers tight end Tucker Kraft said last week that it was good just to get Parsons back into full team drills.

"It's been good out there pressing against Micah," Kraft said. "Took on a bull rush from him [in practice]. He's trying to back me into Jordan [Love's] lap. No comment [on who won the rep]. Maybe it was a stalemate. I'm going to say it's a stalemate. Yeah, he'll be making his return soon. He's looking great, but our defense is rolling, and we just hope that they can remain consistent."

The Packers (6-4) technically have their bye this week, but it's a shortened break because they play on the Wednesday of the following week. In fact, the Packers had to get approval from the league and the NFL Players Association to give their players the mandatory four days off during a bye week after the game against the Rams instead of during their Week 11 bye. LaFleur said the players will have off Tuesday-Thursday this week.

"We'll bring them back in on Friday, and then kind of gear up for the week because Saturday will be like a Wednesday in our world," LaFleur said.

Parsons' return won't solve the offensive line issues that led to their downfall in Sunday's loss to the Minnesota Vikings, who sacked Jordan Love eight times. LaFleur said Monday after reviewing the film that the pass protection was as bad as it looked live.

"It was pretty bad, yeah," LaFleur said. "It wasn't good enough. Certainly some things schematically that we didn't do a good job with and then ultimately there was some execution things as well."

Still, LaFleur said he does not plan to make any staff changes, meaning offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich and offensive line coach Luke Butkus will remain on the job. The Packers had to make a late change to their offensive line after right guard Kevin Zeitler sustained a triceps injury in practice. articles.headline: Vikings WR Jordan Addison needs thumb surgery, is candidate for IR
articles.description: Vikings wide receiver Jordan Addison needs to undergo surgery on his thumb and is a candidate for injured reserve, coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday.
articles.body:
EAGAN, Minn. -- Vikings receiver Jordan Addison could be out for a month because of a thumb injury that will require surgery, coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday.

O'Connell termed it a "freak injury" that occurred while Addison was "catching passes on air" during practice last Friday, aggravating a minor injury Addison had dealt with since training camp. The Vikings listed him as questionable on their injury report and then made him inactive after a short warmup Sunday morning before their 30-10 victory over the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field.

O'Connell said Addison's projected return is "right around hopefully that short-term IR kind of window." Players who are placed on injured reserve must miss at least four games.

"I don't anticipate it being a long-term kind of thing," O'Connell said.

If Addison goes on injured reserve, the earliest he could return is for the Vikings' Week 15 game against the Detroit Lions at U.S. Bank Stadium, scheduled to be played on "Sunday Night Football."

Addison missed the Vikings' Week 5 game against the New Orleans Saints because of a hamstring injury. In seven starts this season, he has caught 18 passes for 277 yards and one touchdown.

With Addison sidelined against the Packers, and veteran Jauan Jennings already declared out because of a calf injury, second-year receiver Tai Felton got his third NFL start alongside Justin Jefferson. Felton caught three passes for 33 yards. Another second-year receiver, Myles Price, caught four passes for 49 yards, including a 38-yard touchdown.

The Vikings waived veteran Odell Beckham Jr. last week but he re-signed to their practice squad and would be available for Sunday's game against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City if needed.

articles.headline: 76ers star LeBron James ruled out vs. Nets due to lower back management
articles.description: LeBron James will miss Monday's game against the Nets as the 76ers continue to manage his lower back.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- LeBron James will miss Monday night's game against the Brooklyn Nets as the Philadelphia 76ers continue to manage his lower back.

The Sixers also announced that star center Joel Embiid, who was out for Sunday's win over the Indiana Pacers, is questionable Monday with right foot plantar fascia issues.

This will be the fourth game missed this season by James, who hasn't played both games in any of the Sixers' back-to-backs this season.

The Sixers are 3-0 without James, with wins over the Charlotte Hornets, Milwaukee Bucks and Toronto Raptors.

In Sunday night's win over the Pacers, James passed Hall of Fame point guard Jason Kidd for third all time on the NBA's career assist list. He finished the game with 15 points, seven rebounds and 11 assists.

James, who turns 42 next month, is averaging 15.1 points, 7.2 rebounds and 6.9 assists per game this season.

Big men Dominick Barlow (back) and Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) were also ruled out for Monday's game.

articles.headline: Fantasy basketball adds and NBA bets: All eyes on Tyrese Maxey on Monday
articles.description: Andre Snellings breaks down Monday's NBA slate, highlighting the fantasy streamers to add and bets to make.
articles.body:
The NBA starts this week with a solid eight-game slate, putting more than half of the league in play. And with yesterday's slate also featuring a robust nine games, we have five teams playing today on the second half of a back-to-back: the Boston Celtics, Houston Rockets, Philadelphia 76ers, Phoenix Suns and Washington Wizards.

The Celtics (37-point win over the Mavericks), Rockets (28-point win over the Wizards) and Wizards (28-point loss to the Rockets) all played in blowouts on Sunday so their starters were largely able to play fewer minutes than usual. This could be vital for the possibility of the veterans on these teams such as Paul George, Kevin Durant or Anthony Davis to be available to play both halves of the back-to-back.

The teams won't necessarily announce their full injury report for tonight's games until later today, but each of those vets has played in at least some back-to-backs this season.

George may be the one to watch the most, as he has missed the second-half of both of the Celtics' last two back-to-back sets. Of the other two teams finishing a back-to-back, the Suns don't have any rotation players that tend to sit one-half of consecutive sets ... but the 76ers do. Joel Embiid and LeBron James have each sat in one half of every back-to-back the 76ers have played this season.

Embiid sat out yesterday, while LeBron played and notched a near triple-double with 15 points, 11 assists and 7 rebounds in 33 minutes. Though he is not currently listed on any injury report for tonight I'd expect that LeBron will sit tonight with Embiid likely returning, though of course you should confirm this and all availability questions once the official reports come out.

These, and many other storylines will be in play for tonight's action. As always, let's dig deeper into the matchups to identify some fantasy streaming options and betting angles of interest from this Monday slate.

But he has particularly picked it up of late as a distributor, averaging 7.4 APG in his last five outings after averaging only 1.9 APG in his first seven games of the season.

Bones Hyland, PG, Minnesota Timberwolves (6.9%)

Hyland is a streaky scorer off the bench that can heat up in a hurry. articles.headline: Bulls' Buzelis, Nets' Minott fined $25K each after making obscene gestures
articles.description: Bulls forward Matas Buzelis and Nets forward Josh Minott have each been fined $25,000 for making obscene gestures toward the stands during their games Saturday.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- Chicago Bulls forward Matas Buzelis and Brooklyn Nets forward Josh Minott have each been fined $25,000 for making obscene gestures toward the stands during their respective games Saturday.

NBA executive vice president and head of basketball operations James Jones announced the fines on Monday.

Buzelis' incident occurred with 11:19 remaining in the fourth quarter of the Bulls' 117-106 win at Minnesota. Minott's gesture happened at the conclusion of the Nets' 129-110 loss at Memphis.

articles.headline: Grizzlies' GG Jackson to miss time with left foot fracture
articles.description: Grizzlies reserve GG Jackson will miss time after breaking a bone in his left foot. He is scheduled to have surgery on the injury.
articles.body:
The Memphis Grizzlies will be without forward GG Jackson after he suffered a broken bone in his foot, the team announced Monday.

Jackson broke the fifth metatarsal in his left foot in the first quarter of Saturday's win over the Brooklyn Nets. He is scheduled to undergo surgery.

A second-round pick of the Grizzlies in 2023, Jackson has found a reserve role on the team.

Jackson is averaging 6.7 points, 3.0 rebounds and 1.0 assist in 15 minutes of action this season for a Grizzlies team that is currently sixth in the Western Conference standings.

articles.headline: Fantasy risers and fallers: Pelicans' Fears provides hope; Harden's numbers down
articles.description: Steve Alexander looks at three players on the rise and three who are slumping and how fantasy managers should react.
articles.body:
Dejounte Murray wants out of New Orleans and probably won't play another game for them, Daniss Jenkins is making noise in Detroit and Sandro Mamukelashvili might become Luka Doncic's new right-hand man if Austin Reaves misses more time.

Meanwhile, Mikal Bridges is getting squeezed in New York, James Harden is starting to show his age and Trey Murphy III hasn't lived up to the preseason expectations.

And even though I didn't write about them below, if Aday Mara, Ausar Thompson or Klay Thompson are still available in your league, they are all worth picking up right now in most leagues.

Risers

 Jeremiah Fears, New Orleans Pelicans, PG/SG (66.6% rostered in ESPN leagues)

Murray has shut it down in New Orleans by demanding a trade, clearing the way for Fears to run the offense until further notice. Maybe they'll trade Murray for a point guard, which would hurt Fears, but if Murray lands in Phoenix or Sacramento, where he's rumored to be drawing interest, there probably isn't a point guard coming back their way with a starting pedigree.

Fears has been great, scoring in double digits in 12 straight games, playing 33.5 minutes in his last two, and racking up production in scoring, rebounds, assists, steals and 3-pointers on a nightly basis. He's also not likely to turn the ball over much and was playing very well, even when Murray was still a part of the picture. The second-year standout is simply a must-roster player the rest of the season.

 Daniss Jenkins, Detroit Pistons, PG (31.7% rostered)

Jenkins was plopped into the starting unit a week ago and while it remains to be seen what happens once Jalen Duren (hamstring) returns, I'd like to believe that John Collins will go to the bench and Jenkins will stick in the starting unit.

The Pistons need his ball-handling skills on the court to complement Cade Cunningham, and Jenkins has played very strong for the last four games (since he moved into the starting unit). Jenkins has averaged 21.0 points, 4.5 rebounds, 4.3 assists, 2.3 steals, 3.5 3-pointers and just 1.0 turnovers over his last four games. Granted, his scoring has dropped in each of those four games (31, 22, 21 and 10) but I don't care. He's really good.

Doncic seems to trust Mamu and loves kicking it out to him for open threes when Luka's not actually shooting the ball himself. articles.body:
Incoming Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino is eyeing a quick reunion with USMNT midfielder Weston McKennie, while Atlético Madrid are exploring a deal for Lisandro Martínez.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United are interested in United States men's national team midfielder Weston McKennie, according to La Gazzetta dello Sport. Incoming head coach Mauricio Pochettino admires the 28-year-old's versatility after working with him with the USMNT and could seek a reunion at Old Trafford. However, McKennie's club, Juventus, see him as central to head coach Luciano Spalletti's plans and are reluctant to sanction a January departure. His contract runs until June 2030.

- Fulham defender Calvin Bassey is expected to feature prominently among Manchester United's January targets under Pochettino, according to The Telegraph. The incoming head coach wants to strengthen his backline, with Bassey's pace and ability to cover at full back making him an attractive option. The Nigeria international's contract runs until next summer, although Fulham hold an option to extend it by a further 12 months.

- Chelsea continue to track Kerim Alajbegović, having come close to signing him before his summer move to Juventus, La Gazzetta dello Sport has revealed. The Serie A giants are determined to resist any efforts to lure him away from Turin. Alajbegović, 19, is contracted until 2031 and remains -- much like McKennie -- a key member of Spalletti's Juve squad. At this stage, no formal negotiations have taken place between the two clubs.

- Atlético Madrid are exploring a January move for Manchester United defender Lisandro Martínez, as per TEAMtalk. Diego Simeone's side are attracted by the prospect of pairing the 28-year-old with his Argentine teammate Cristian Romero, although Barcelona are also interested. Martínez has indicated he wants to leave United in 2027 and favours a move to Spain, with the Premier League club open to his departure as they look to reshape their squad.

- Brighton & Hove Albion, Bayer Leverkusen and RB Leipzig are pursuing Juventus midfielder Adin Licina ahead of January, Tuttosport reports. The teenager is on loan at Cremonese, and Juventus remain reluctant to let him leave permanently before assessing his potential at Serie A level. Bayern Munich retain a preferential right and a 30% share of any future transfer fee.

articles.headline: Meet Como's Nico Paz, the heir to Lionel Messi's Argentina No. 10 shirt
articles.description: Como's Nico Paz has become one of the best young players in Europe, but now he faces the unenviable task of stepping into Lionel Messi's Argentina No. 10 shirt.
articles.body:
Como's Nico Paz has become one of the best young players in Europe this season, but now he faces the unenviable task of stepping into the Argentina No. 10 shirt worn by the legendary Lionel Messi.

Paz is the son of Pablo Paz, who played for Argentina at the 1998 World Cup, and was born in Tenerife, Spain. He began his senior career at Real Madrid and spent three years with their B team, RM Castilla, but struggled to break into the first team. He made his debut in January 2022 -- and his international debut came a few months later -- yet only managed eight first-team appearances in all competitions before leaving for Como in August 2024 for around €6 million, though his contract included various clauses allowing Madrid to re-sign him.

Under former Barcelona, Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder Cesc Fàbregas, himself in his first senior coaching job at Como, Paz developed incredibly. "He taught me practically everything," Paz told UEFA earlier this year. "I arrived here as a young player from Castilla. I'd played a few games for Real Madrid, but in the end I was a reserve-team player in a lower division.

"Coming here and playing in Serie A, the top flight, allowed me to grow and improve a lot, both as a player and as a person. It was all thanks to Cesc, who believed in me and brought me here. From the first day he let me play the way I wanted and gave me a lot of freedom. He taught me a lot. I think the player I am today is all down to him."

His form for Como took off and he has scored 25 goals and made 25 assists in his 89 games so far -- six goals and eight assists from 14 games this season. Obviously that saw plenty of transfer links, including to Arsenal and Chelsea, but a complicated deal saw Madrid agree to let Como take on his full rights for around €60 million this summer, with a clause for them to re-sign the player for €80 million in 2027 if they wish.

So who is Argentina's heir to Messi, now that the great man has retired from international football? And what do we need to know about his style of play? Sam Tighe and Tor-Kristian Karlsen explore.

Can Nico Paz replace Lionel Messi for Argentina?

Comparing anyone to arguably the greatest player the world has ever seen can feel cruel, but it's a rite of passage any young creative Argentine player must undertake -- particularly in the wake of Messi's international retirement and the fact that Paz will take over his No. 10 shirt.

In the seasons they turned 21 (and played a full campaign), Messi racked up 34 league goals contributions for Barcelona in 2008-09 -- the season that saw Barcelona win the Champions League and Messi score in the 2-0 win in the final. That split into 23 goals and 11 assists, and he overperformed his expected goals tally (11.85) by a huge margin.

articles.headline: Mauricio Pochettino to Man United: Is Tottenham love affair finally over?
articles.description: Mauricio Pochettino is back in the Premier League as the new Man United boss. For Tottenham fans, it's complicated.
articles.headlineJa: マウリシオ・ポチェッティーノがマンUへ：トッテナムとの愛の物語はついに終わるのか？
articles.descriptionJa: マウリシオ・ポチェッティーノがマンチェスター・ユナイテッドの新監督としてプレミアリーグに復帰します。トッテナムのファンにとっては、複雑な心境となるでしょう。
articles.body:
"He's magic, you know, Mauricio Pochettino!" For five years, these were the words that rang out amongst Tottenham fans.

First, at the old White Hart Lane -- a much-loved, if dilapidated, ground that became a fortress during Pochettino's years as head coach of the club. Then, at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium -- a magnificent arena that, in recent years, has felt more like a house of horrors than any sort of stronghold.

But now Pochettino is back in the Premier League, this time as Manchester United manager. And for Tottenham fans who once dreamed of seeing the Argentine return to north London, it's another reminder that the man who gave us so many unforgettable memories might never be coming home.

The Pochettino love affair

The Argentine manager joined Tottenham in 2014 and was at the helm of one of the best, and most beloved, Spurs teams in the club's history. Under Pochettino, Harry Kane (now a Ballon d'Or winner!), Son Heung-Min, Christian Eriksen, Dele Alli, Jan Vertonghen, Toby Alderweireld, Mousa Dembélé and Hugo Lloris all shone in ways that few football fans and pundits expected.

During the Pochettino era, Tottenham came agonisingly close to winning the Premier League and reached the Champions League final. They went an entire season unbeaten at home -- somewhat unthinkable now given the team's struggles at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium -- and played some of the most thrilling football in the league at the time.

There were famous victories over arch-rivals Arsenal and in Europe, including over Real Madrid and Borussia Dortmund, and, of course, there was that night in Amsterdam. When Lucas Moura scored an astonishing hat trick against Ajax to send Spurs to the Champions League final for the first time in our history.

For many Spurs fans, including myself, the Poch years brought some of our best ever memories of supporting the club. There was a special connection between Pochettino and fans. He was revered and many of us hoped that it would last forever -- even if we all knew that, really, nothing ever lasts that long. Especially not in football.

When Pochettino was sacked, rather unceremoniously, in November 2019 -- just months after taking us to the Champions League final -- it felt somewhat unjust.

It was clear for anyone to see in 2019 that Tottenham's squad was beginning to get stale in a number of areas and that what the club truly needed was a rebuild. For myriad reasons, that never came to fruition and so, when, results on the pitch took a nosedive in the winter of that year the axe fell on Pochettino.

Overnight, the man who had turned Tottenham into a truly formidable side capable of beating anyone on their day was gone. Since then, it's fair to say that no other manager that has taken the wheel at the club has managed to form the same sort of bond that Pochettino had with us.

Many have come and gone but it hasn't yet felt like any of them have "got" us the way that Pochettino did. It is early days under Roberto De Zerbi

articles.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is holding off on signing a new contract for now, while Arsenal are the latest team to join a long list of admirers following Middlesbrough striker Will Lankshear. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is holding off on signing a new contract for now, says The Sun. Fernandes, 32, has a contract which expires next summer -- albeit with a one-year club option to renew -- and reportedly wants to wait to see what happens under new boss Mauricio Pochettino. The Portugal midfielder has been linked with a lucrative move to Saudi Arabia before.

- Arsenal are in the market for a center forward, and TEAMtalk claims that the Gunners are the latest team to join a long list of admirers following Middlesbrough striker Will Lankshear. The 21-year-old joined Boro from Tottenham Hotspur this summer, after a loan spell at Oxford United in the Championship, and has hit the ground running, scoring 13 goals in as many appearances in the league so far. That has brought about plenty of transfer interest, but Middlesbrough will try to block any exit in January.

- Arsenal are continuing the push to sign a left-sided forward, with RB Leipzig star Antonio Nusa leading their shortlist, says TEAMtalk. Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard left in the summer, and were replaced by Christos Tzolis before a move to sign Vinícius Júnior from Real Madrid fell short. With Mikel Arteta wanting more options on that flank, the report claims that talks have opened with Nusa's representatives about a possible switch, but the 21-year-old's transfer could cost €80 million.

- Tottenham defender Pedro Porro has decided that he only wants to join Barcelona if he leaves the club, according to Sport. The 27-year-old Spain right back has seen interest from the Blaugrana, as well as Real Madrid, despite only signing a new contract with Spurs in the summer. But while Barcelona are eyeing up a deal worth no more than €50 million next summer, Tottenham will stand firm on their €70 million valuation.

- AC Milan are looking to bolster in the forward areas during January, with Gazzetta dello Sport reporting that Real Madrid's Endrick and Club Brugge's Nicolò Tresoldi are on their shortlist. Endrick has seen few minutes in the starting XI for Los Blancos this season and Milan are keen on a loan deal with a permanent option included. Meanwhile, Tresoldi  22, who has five goals in four Champions League appearances this season, has caught the eye of a number of a teams and could move in a €60 million deal.

Other rumors

- Arsenal believe that Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior will join the club eventually. (Football Transfers)

- Sunderland will look to block any move for Brian Brobbey, as Tottenham are eyeing a potential deal for the striker. (Football Insider)
